scope_depth_novelty.assessment: The 1,477-word report answers one finite question: scalar FP32 score staging for a 16x32 logical tile. It traces matrix-apply writes and scalar max/sum reads, contrasts pitch32 control with pitch33 padding and two alternative maps, preserves BF16 Q/K/V/P, FP32 accumulation/online state and reduction/update order, and gives bounded opposite-outcome decision rules.
scope_depth_novelty.novelty: This is distinct from R568 head-tile/SLM work and R945/R947 adjacent-query union and N64 staging. The prior review/index record no local score-pitch measurement or adoption; R948 isolates only the scalar score address map.
scope_depth_novelty.depth: Good for decision support: alternatives include mapping/bijection, producer and consumer implications, resource cost, numerical boundaries, measurement plan, source provenance and counterevidence. The public-source gap is explicitly stated.
scope_depth_novelty.source_contract: The report correctly treats score SLM bank arithmetic as conditional on a simple interleave model, not a measured B570 bank map. It does not attribute the existing nonexclusive profile to SLM conflicts or claim occupancy/XMX/VRAM saturation.

local_source_check.check: Source hash matches R948. It declares scores as scalar local_accessor<float,1>, writes matrix-apply coordinates into that array, and reads rows for sequential max/sum. Matrix load operands are BF16 qtile/kv and probability/kv. The header’s “No production caller” statement limits applicability to a diagnostic component.
local_source_check.logical_payload: Source declares 28,160 bytes and a +4,096-byte device-local-memory admission margin. Pitch33 would add 64 logical bytes to 28,224; physical allocation rounding and device admission remain unknown.
local_source_check.measurement_boundary: Main supplied that its pitch33-only 6-process comparison is active and must not be consumed partially. Main’s 11 structural/numerical cases, including the physical 262,144-context cases, passed; those results do not establish speed. The suggested five-process-per-arm plan is superseded while that same candidate comparison runs.
local_source_check.matrix_alignment_limit: Matrix extension requires matrix-load/store base pointers to be 4-byte aligned. Source offsets and element strides are multiples of 4/8 bytes, but the source/spec citations do not alone prove each local_accessor<BFloat> base pointer alignment; retain this implementation-level check. This does not change the score-only candidate mapping.

operational_corrections.correction: R948 calls qsa_bf16_prefix.cpp the production source/current path. Its header says “No production caller.” Treat the report as guidance for the diagnostic kernel/component only; trace the configured build’s actual production caller before making production performance or adoption claims.

The statement that pitch33 has “no extra arithmetic in the addressing expressions” is not established. Row pitch 33 can change index arithmetic and lowering versus pitch32. Compare generated code or compiler reports before treating address cost as unchanged.

The proposed five-process-per-arm score-pitch comparison is redundant while Main’s clean six-process pitch33 comparison is active. Do not consume partial timings or duplicate the cohort. After closure, only repeat or expand if the result leaves a concrete question.

28,224 bytes is the pitch33 logical payload estimate after adding 64 bytes to the source’s 28,160; it is not a B570 allocation, occupancy, admission or performance result. Account for the source guard’s +64 logical bytes, then verify actual device/compiler behavior.

The supplied 89.2009-second wrapper and 21.5123-second attention-plus-prefixpack intervals are nonexclusive and lack PMU/physical VRAM/PCIe/XMX/SLM-counter evidence. Treat any pitch benefit as a component measurement, not a bank-conflict or whole-prefill attribution.

The reported matrix operand offsets and byte strides meet their multiples, but the 4-byte base-pointer requirement is separate. The local source does not explicitly establish the local_accessor<BFloat> base alignment; retain compiler/runtime confirmation before treating operand alignment as source-proven. This is orthogonal to the score-only pitch experiment.

The cited Khronos sycl-2020.html URL is a live page that currently serves revision 12, not an immutable revision URL. The local_accessor claim is supported, but pin the revision when this source is retrieved as frozen evidence.
